$description: COBALT TOKENS. The one source of truth for colour, elevation, type, spacing, motion, stacking and layout on every app on this standard, in two first-class modes (dark is the base, light is a token swap with no component branching). Every colour literal in an app lives here and nowhere else. Contrast is certified by tokens/build.py and listed in tokens/CONTRAST.md.

surfaces.$description: A blue-dark luminance ladder, all leaning ~218deg. Dark steps UP in lightness as elevation rises. The canvas is not black on purpose: a soft accent wash sits behind the shell, and pure black kills it. --surface-inset moves OPPOSITE the raised ladder, to near-black, because an inset well recedes. Measured relative luminance: inset 0.00240, canvas 0.00335, s1 0.01057, s2 0.01816, s3 0.02587, s4 0.03002, s5 0.04712. Card over canvas 1.135, raised panel over card 1.125. Steps 4 and 5 stay close to step 3 on purpose: coloured status text must still clear 4.5:1 on the hover and pressed surfaces.
surfaces.$light_description: Light mode is NOT a mirror of the dark ladder. Cards and panels (--surface-1) are white on a light grey canvas, so content reads as raised paper, and the border plus the elevation shadow carry the separation instead of a darker fill. The steps above surface-1 descend from white for the states that sit on a card: --surface-2 for table heads, modal feet and secondary buttons, --surface-3 for hover and chips (a step darker than the canvas, so hover shows on the canvas and on a card), --surface-4 and --surface-5 for pressed and selected. The inset well stays white with the field border. Measured relative luminance: canvas 0.8029, s1 1.0000, s2 0.9193, s3 0.7403, s4 0.6600, s5 0.5722, inset 1.0000. Card over canvas 1.231. Hover (--surface-3) clears the canvas and the card, so a hover reads on both.

canvas-rgb.$description: RGB triplets, for the two places that need an alpha composite of a surface. You cannot put a hex custom property inside rgba(); use these instead, or color-mix().
canvas-rgb.$light_description: RGB triplets, for the two places that need an alpha composite of a surface.

body-wash.$description: Ambient wash. One fixed radial, applied to a pointer-events:none ::before on body so it never intercepts a click.

elevation.$description: Six concrete steps. Every step = a hairline ring + one or two same-angle key shadows with NEGATIVE spread + a 1px top inner highlight. Same angle throughout (straight down), so the family reads as one light source above.
elevation.$light_description: Identical geometry, identical angle, identical negative spreads, same six steps. Only the colours mirror: the hairline ring goes from white to the deep navy ink, the key shadows soften and take that same navy, and the 1px top inner highlight goes to a strong white, which is what reads as milled on a tinted light surface. A white hairline is invisible on a light surface, which is why the ring inverts rather than carrying over.

card-sheen.$description: A faint top light on a card face, painted as a background-image so it sits over the fill. Dark only, light sets it to none because a white card has no light to add.

header-wash.$description: A soft tint of the active accent that fades across a page title block. It reads the accent channel triplet, so it follows data-app-accent with no extra wiring. Always layered over a surface and framed by a full hairline, never an edge bar.

canvas-wash.$description: One soft radial of the active accent behind the content, painted over the canvas colour on the app shell root. Never a pattern. Follows data-app-accent through the accent channel triplet.

scrim.$description: The one overlay scrim. Every frosted backdrop uses it.

shadow-xs.$description: Small key shadow under raised controls: the selected tab, the segmented thumb, the nav marker.

shadow-key.$description: Key shadow paired with the hue glow under hero stat tiles.

shadow-lift.$description: Hover lift for small floating cards.

shadow-pop.$description: Deep shadow for panels floating over content: the command palette, popovers.

backdrop.$description: Dimming layer behind command surfaces that must read as the only thing on screen (the command palette). Dims in both modes, unlike --scrim.

sheen.$description: The light streak of a sweep: the build card sheen, skeleton shimmer.

borders.$description: Ratios measured against --bg-canvas: subtle 1.34, default 2.05, strong 3.14. Against the card: 1.18, 1.81, 2.76.
borders.$light_description: Measured against the light canvas: subtle 1.13, default 1.57, strong 2.23. Against the white card: 1.39, 1.94, 2.75. On a white card the default border is the line that separates the card from the canvas, with --elev-1 under it.

border-field.$description: the GATED form-control boundary, at least 3:1 on every surface a field can sit on. A visible label tells you a field exists but not where to click, so WCAG 1.4.11 applies and --border-default does not clear it against the field fill. --border-default keeps its role for labelled controls and container outlines, where the label and the fill do the identifying.
border-field.$light_description: the GATED form-control boundary, at least 3:1 on every surface a field can sit on.

text.$description: Ratios measured against --surface-1 (#121a2d), and certified against every surface the ink can sit on.
text.$light_description: Ratios measured against --surface-1 (#ffffff, the white card), and certified against every surface the ink can sit on.

text-tertiary.$description: meta, timestamps, eyebrows, 8.86:1 on --surface-1 and at least 5.5:1 on every surface. A tertiary meta cell inside a hoverable row lands on --bg-hover, so the floor is the interaction surfaces, not --surface-1.
text-tertiary.$light_description: meta, timestamps, eyebrows, 10.14:1 on --surface-1 and at least 6:1 on every surface

text-quaternary.$description: the lowest-emphasis text, glyphs and separators. Clears 4.5:1 on the page, the card and the raised panel (--surface-2): 7.2:1, 6.34:1 and 5.63:1. On the hover and pressed surfaces it falls toward 4:1, so keep real copy on the other three inks there.
text-quaternary.$light_description: the lowest-emphasis text, glyphs and separators. Clears 4.5:1 on the page, the card and the raised panel: 5.00:1, 6.16:1 and 5.69:1.

text-inverse.$description: on the accent or danger fill, 5.23:1 on --accent. The SAME value in light mode, because the fill is the same colour in both modes.

text-on-accent.$description: the name an app reaches for on any accent fill (a selected chip, a primary badge). It is --text-inverse, so it is certified with it.

accent.$description: The logo blue. The NUMBERED ramp is a scale, 50 lightest through 800 darkest, and it is byte-identical in both modes. Only the ROLE aliases re-point per mode: in dark they take the light end of the ramp, in light the dark end. 500 is the sampled peak, 600 is the brand token and the fill, and the FILL never moves, so the primary CTA is pixel-identical in both modes.
accent.$light_description: The numbered ramp is a SCALE and is byte-identical to dark: 50 lightest through 800 darkest, monotonic. Only the ROLE aliases re-point, from the light end of the ramp to the dark end. The FILL does not move at all, so the primary CTA is pixel-identical in both modes, which is the strongest cohesion the two-mode system has.

accent-rgb.$description: The accent identity hue (step 500) as an RGB triplet, for alpha tints and glows: rgb(var(--accent-rgb) / 0.2). Mode-invariant.

accent-600.$description: brand token: fills and gradient end

accent-hover.$description: hover LIGHTENS in dark, and darkens in light. Keeps white at 4.59:1 on the face, and its luminance 0.1787 against --accent-600's 0.1507 so the hover still reads as a lift.
accent-hover.$light_description: hover DARKENS in light, lightens in dark. Both keep white at 4.5:1 on the face: 7.17:1 here.

accent-bright.$light_description: the accent text/icon ink. The name says its ROLE, not its lightness.

accent-dim.$description: --accent-dim is OPAQUE, like every --<tone>-dim, so the one accent chip that carries text has a single certified ratio instead of a different one per surface behind it. An alpha wash composited over --surface-4 or --surface-5 dropped --accent-bright to 4.31:1 and 3.89:1. This value is the old 16% wash resolved over --surface-1, its commonest base, so nothing shifts visually.
accent-dim.$light_description: --accent-dim is OPAQUE in both modes, like every --<tone>-dim, so the one accent chip that carries text has a single certified ratio instead of a different one per surface behind it. This value is the old 12% wash composited over --surface-1, its commonest base.

accent-rgb-d.$description: Deep stop (step 700) as a triplet, for deep tiles that carry white text.

accent-fill.$description: Primary fill face (step 600) as a triplet. White text clears 4.5:1 on it in both modes.

accent-fill-d.$description: Primary fill base (step 700) as a triplet, the gradient and pressed end.

accent-seed.$description: The exact brand colour the accent was built from. Identity marks only (favicon, brand tile, logo). Never text and never a fill that carries text: use the certified ramp for those.

accent-withheld-hue.$description: The categorical hue this accent collides with, which an app must not use as a data colour (the kit palette helper drops it). none when there is no collision.

status.$description: Mapped to the logo inks. Ratios on --surface-1. The four inks are also placed for DEUTERANOPIA separation: simulated worst pair is 12.4 CIEDE2000. Colour is never the only channel regardless.
status.$light_description: Dark inks on light tints. Ratios on --surface-1. These are NOT the dark values darkened one for one: they are placed on a deliberate luminance staircase, because in light mode all four inks must be dark, which collapses them into one region of the deuteranopia-simulated space. Worst simulated pair here is 12.3 CIEDE2000.

urgent.$description: Urgent (high priority) ink, the orange step between --warning and --danger. Certified 4.5:1 or better on every content surface and on its tint. Under simulated deuteranopia it sits about 7.5 CIEDE2000 from warning and 9 from danger, closer than the four original inks, so an urgent mark always carries a label too.
urgent.$light_description: Urgent ink, dark orange on light, between the warning and danger inks on the luminance staircase. Simulated deuteranopia puts it about 5.2 CIEDE2000 from warning and 5.7 from danger, so an urgent mark always carries a label too.

danger.$description: Danger ink. Certified 4.5:1 or better on canvas, inset and surfaces 1 to 4 (hover rows included), see CONTRAST.md.
danger.$light_description: Danger ink, dark on light. Same certification as dark mode.

danger-border.$description: also the GATED invalid-field state border, at least 3:1 on every field surface. aria-invalid plus a message is not enough when the border is specified as a state indicator.
danger-border.$light_description: also the GATED invalid-field state border, 3.72:1 to 4.94:1 on every field surface

danger-hover.$description: destructive TEXT hover: lightens in dark, darkens in light. A fill step is DARKER, so hovering a danger label onto --danger-700 made it less readable, at 3.11:1 on --bg-card.
danger-hover.$light_description: destructive TEXT hover: darkens in light, lightens in dark. New in both modes.

on-fill.$description: Inks and overlays for content on a deep tile or the accent fill. Those surfaces are dark in both modes, so these values are mode-invariant. Text inks are certified at the gloss peak of every deep tile.
on-fill.$light_description: Same ~218deg lean, descending ladder. Measured relative luminance: 0.9108, 0.8594, 0.8035, 0.7408, 0.6606, 0.5727, and 1.0000 for the inset well. Adjacent steps: 1.093, 1.057, 1.065, 1.079, 1.113, 1.141, which brackets the dark ladder's 1.031 to 1.123.

on-fill-gloss.$description: Top-left gloss stop of the tile gradient, the lightest point of the tile.

on-fill-shade.$description: Bottom-right shade stop of the tile gradient.

focus.$description: Inner ring in the surface colour separates the halo from the element; outer ring is the lifted accent at 90% alpha, which composites to between 3.90:1 and 5.64:1 against every one of the seven surfaces, not just against --surface-1. The old rgba(36,134,185,0.85) measured 3.56:1 on --surface-1 but only 2.90:1 on --surface-4 and 2.66:1 on --surface-5, so a focused control on a hovered or pressed row had no conformant ring.
focus.$light_description: Same two-ring structure. Inner ring in the surface colour separates the halo from the element; outer ring is a dark accent at 92% alpha, which composites to between 3.75:1 and 5.95:1 against every one of the seven surfaces, not just against --surface-1. The dark ring at 85% of the mid accent measured 2.66:1 on --bg-active, so both modes needed a new outer colour.

spacing.$description: 4px base. Ten steps, all of them listed.

fs-title.$description: role step, same size as --fs-h1: a page or panel title

fs-subtitle.$description: role step: a subtitle under a title

fw-medium.$description: medium weight: controls and quiet emphasis

fw-semibold.$description: semibold weight: labels, titles and the default emphasis

fw-bold.$description: bold weight: strong titles and figures

motion.$description: Five interaction durations, a choreography scale for entrances, travel and loops, and five curves. Exits are shorter than entrances (a dialog enters on --dur-slower and exits on --dur-base). No raw ms anywhere else in the codebase (ui_lint UI005). Decorative assets (illustrations, mascots) may declare their own timing variables once at the asset root.

dur-slow.$description: Layout moves such as the rail expanding.

dur-travel.$description: Elements that travel: sheets, toasts, gliding markers, spring settles.

dur-enter.$description: Content entrances: fade up, staggered lists, table rows, empty-state icons.

dur-chart.$description: Chart bars growing in and hero number count-up.

dur-spin.$description: One turn of the working spinner. Reduced motion holds the ring still.

dur-pulse.$description: One beat of the live heartbeat. Every live indicator shares it.

stagger-step.$description: Delay between siblings in a staggered entrance.

stacking.$description: ONE ladder. Every layered element takes its number from here; a raw z-index literal is a violation.

z-base.$description: the app shell and page content

z-content.$description: content that must clear the ambient layer

z-sticky.$description: sticky table head, sticky filter bar

aliases.$description: Older component code uses these names. They are aliases, not second definitions: one value, two spellings, so a tool recolours by editing the ladder above and nothing else. They are also MODE-INVARIANT: each one is a var() indirection, so it follows its target into light mode. Never restate this table inside the light override.

categorical.$description: Six hues for data in a fixed series rotation, never for brand, plus two extra hues (yellow and ink) that data takes only by name and that never enter the rotation, the avatar hash or the accent withholding. Each is a bright identity triplet (marks, icons, series) plus a deep stop that holds white text at 4.5:1 in both modes. Light values are darker so marks clear 3:1 on light surfaces.

hue-blue.$description: Bright identity triplets are for marks, icons and chart series. Use as rgb(var(--hue-blue)).

hue-blue-d.$description: Deep stops are tile fills that carry white text.

hue-amber-d.$description: Deep amber tile stop at OKLCH L 0.47, in line with the other deep stops, so tile text passes at the gloss peak.

hue-yellow.$description: Extra hue, outside the series rotation: yellow for data that is yellow by name (a yellow toner, a yellow flag). Light is an olive gold so the mark clears 3:1 on white.

hue-yellow-d.$description: Deep yellow tile stop that holds white text.

hue-ink.$description: Extra hue, outside the series rotation: the solid neutral ink for data that is black by name (black toner, a neutral series). Near black in light. In dark it is a light slate, because a black mark cannot clear 3:1 on a dark surface: the mark keeps its place as the darkest-in-print, lightest-on-screen neutral.

hue-ink-d.$description: Deep neutral tile stop that holds white text.

glow-a.$description: Alpha of the one glow recipe. Theme-gated: strong in dark, faint in light.

prose.$description: Long-form reading surfaces (documents, articles). Mode-invariant. --text-prose is an alias, not a fifth ink: if halation on long documents ever needs a softer ink, add it as a certified pair, never a single-mode hex.

accents.$description: Named per-app accents. An app sets one on the root (data-app-accent). Each is generated from its seed in the seed hue with this lightness and chroma profile, then certified: white on the fill, the text ink on every content surface and on the chip, the focus ring on every surface, in both modes.

cobalt.$description: The default. Hand-tuned: its values are the accent group above, so it needs no attribute.

hub.$description: The original hub orange, kept by name for apps that already set it.

rules.why: Body, supporting and meta text on every surface
Lowest-emphasis text and glyphs (quaternary ink) on the page, the card and the raised panel
Coloured text on content and hover surfaces
White text on the solid success, warning and danger buttons
Subtle success and warning button ink on its tint
Accent text on the accent chip
Success badge ink on its tint
Warning badge ink on its tint
Urgent badge ink on its tint
Danger badge ink on its tint
Info badge ink on its tint
Form control boundary and invalid state (WCAG 1.4.11)
Focus ring outer edge on every surface
Categorical marks and icons on content surfaces (non-text, 3:1)
Text on deep tiles at the gloss peak, the lightest point of the tile
